whatItFakes: Every filing window opens July 1 of the preceding year.
why: The legacy field-entry helper uses one estimated opening bound for every place and office.
replacement: Dated place-specific filing window facts, selected by the port.

whatItFakes: Uses the legacy 30-day elector residence rule for every supplied elector requirement.
why: The original qualification helper applies a single-place legal figure without checking whether other place facts agree. Preserve this suspected bug.
replacement: Per-place voter residence facts with explicit legal dates; CTO decides the change.

whatItFakes: Subtracts 1e-9 before rounding a percentage signature count upward.
why: The legacy helper uses this tolerance. Preserve it pending the integer arithmetic contract.
replacement: Sourced signature rounding rule and a checked exact arithmetic implementation.

whatItFakes: Contiguous household roster positions stand in for ward geography and population, with a common ten-percent deviation bound.
why: Legacy drawWardCuts uses household counts and positions, not geographic population. Preserve its output and member protection unchanged.
replacement: Caller-supplied geographic population units and place-specific legal deviation bounds.

whatItFakes: Salary uses 52 weeks and tenure uses 365.25 days per year.
why: Legacy salary annualization and tenure arithmetic use fixed calendar averages.
replacement: Reviewed payroll cadence and calendar-year service facts.

whatItFakes: Office salary is a reciprocal-rank regional/income comparison rounded to hundreds with at least four donors.
why: The authored estimator is preserved without replacing it with a researched salary.
replacement: Sourced office pay or reviewed salary estimation parameters.

whatItFakes: Population rank chooses at-large/ward/mixed composition from national survey shares where the charter is unread.
why: Legacy assigns national patterns by town size and uses a national mixed-seat fraction.

whatItFakes: Addresses are absent; precinct populations apportion people in roster order, with a state/pooled mean where VTD counts are missing.
why: Preserve address-free population shares, largest remainders, census year-after timing and deficit-based arrivals.
replacement: Recorded addresses, dated precinct boundaries and census/arrival adapters.

whatItFakes: Unread towns use the national modal direct-election/four-year Mayor profile, with the owner interim population gate.
why: The legal reading wins; all inherited typical and owner-interim behavior is preserved.
replacement: Dated local executive title, selection and term facts.

whatItFakes: A term search checks at most sixteen election years backward.
why: Preserve the legacy finite guard and error.
replacement: Reviewed calendar coverage bounds or a direct legal cycle calculation.

whatItFakes: Continuity age compares month/day strings, so a leap-day birthday advances on March 1 in a common year.
why: Other legacy age helpers advance on February 28. Keep continuity behavior unchanged.

whatItFakes: A stable-key FNV offset walks the whole person roster, rather than recorded contact geography.
why: This controls which conversations are offered, not the sign/decline decision; preserve the legacy order.
replacement: Recorded canvassing route and contact availability facts.

whatItFakes: Missing term-end tags retain a null value cast as a date by the legacy occupant reader.
why: Do not repair the legacy malformed-record behavior during extraction.
replacement: Reviewed record validation and explicit missing-term evidence handling.
